sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: 'We don't pay' - lawyer advises how to avoid £45,000 illegal-worker fine The Home Office has launched an investigation after a solicitor was secretly filmed by the BBC explaining how he could make a £45,000 illegal-working fine go away.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Mohammad Alias Yousaf - also known as Alias - made the claim to an undercover reporter, who was posing as a mini-mart owner facing a fine for employing an illegal worker.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has said it will also examine the BBC's findings to see whether there has been misconduct by solicitors or law firms.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: The Bradford-based solicitor told his potential client he could avoid paying the fine if he was able to find someone overseas prepared to declare themselves the owner of the mini-mart.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Yousaf has denied ever providing such advice to anyone, or giving false information to the Home Office.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: The BBC's wider investigation also revealed at least £150m is currently owed to the government in uncollected illegal-working fines, according to Home Office figures exclusively obtained by the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: In response, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood ordered a review of the way such fines are issued and collected.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Mahmood said she wanted to thank the BBC "for exposing those who undermine our rules".
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: "Illegal working undermines honest employers, undercuts local wages, and fuels organised immigration crime," she added.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Watch the full film of Ed Thomas's investigation here , external The Home Office said it would be investigating the allegations to see whether there had been a breach of immigration rules.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Senior politicians have since called UK immigration enforcement "weak" and a "laughing stock".
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Shadow home secretary Chris Philp has called for Yousaf to be "struck off as a solicitor", while shadow justice minister Nick Timothy has written to the head of the regulator for solicitors to take "urgent action, and stop Mr Yousaf practising as a solicitor".
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Philp said: "Shabana Mahmood likes to boast about how many fines are issued, but now it turns out most just get ignored.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: She said she had seen immigration fine notices, "some worth £40,000, stuffed in a box" on a mini-mart counter.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Our undercover reporter, who pretended to have a £45,000 illegal working fine, secretly recorded Yousaf saying he could transfer the penalty into someone else's name for a fee of £4,500.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: Yousaf has denied ever advising anyone to put a penalty into the name of someone who was not responsible for a business, or to give false information to the Home Office, and said he never would.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: "My work is to challenge penalties lawfully, through the routes Parliament has provided, usually on the basis that the person found was not an employee at all," Yousaf told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: He added that when our reporter proposed putting his business into someone else's name, Yousaf had told him in writing he could not advance an untruthful or dishonest case and did not act for him.
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: The government said "arrests and raids are at their highest ever levels and removals of illegal workers up 50%".
sentences.article_title: Home Office investigating after BBC catches lawyer offering to make fines go away

sentences.text: A US midterms voter poll has suggested data centres were a highly motivating issue for many Americans, leading some to argue public backlash against the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure construction boom might have helped shape the election outcome.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has looked at its role in the campaign and examined the potential consequences for the AI industry.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: The poll for AP and a consortium of news organisations found 56% of surveyed voters said data centres were a "crucial or major" factor in their vote, while 76% said they would oppose the construction of a new data centre in their community.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: The hostile sentiment was considerably stronger among those who said they voted Democrat at this election.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: This follows other recent Pew Research polling , external which suggested about half of Americans think data centres are "mostly bad" for the environment, home energy costs and quality of life, a big deterioration in favourability since January.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: The congressional voter poll results certainly suggest a remarkable degree of salience for a subject which likely would not have been on most Americans' radar five years ago.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: However, it is some way behind several key issues people considered a "crucial or major factor" in their vote, including government corruption (90%) and the cost of living (89%).
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: Three of the Senate seats flipped by the Democrats have significantly more data centres , external , Texas (595), Ohio (258) and Iowa (117), than the median of 55 across all 50 states.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: And Texas alone has 31 ongoing data centre construction projects, the most of any state , external .
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: But other factors would also have been motivating voters in these states, as elsewhere.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: BBC Verify analysis of state-level voter polling for Senate elections suggests states which swung to the Democrats either followed the national trend over data centre concerns, or seemed less concerned.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: So we can't say how many votes or Senate seats were directly delivered by data centre opposition.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: Official data , external shows inflation-adjusted monthly spending on building data centres, excluding the IT hardware to go into them, in August 2026 was $5bn (£4.2bn) - five times higher than in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: Analysis by Columbia Business School , external suggests AI infrastructure investment in the US is currently larger as a share of the overall economy than spending on new railways was at the height of that boom in the 19th Century.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: Cori Crider, executive director of the Future of Tech Institute, a European think tank, told BBC Verify the industry should anticipate that new state leaders will put conditions on or "even stop runaway data centre build".
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: Seema Shah, from global investment firm Principal Asset Management, said requirements for developers to pay for additional investment in the electricity grid, meet tougher standards over their usage of resources like water, or give up tax incentives could "raise development costs and slow new supply".
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: The Stargate Oracle AI data centre spans roughly four million square feet in Abilene, Texas However, Heather West from the Eurasia Group consultancy said temporary bans on construction and new regulations might delay the data centre roll out, but would not stop it entirely.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: She said "projects already permitted or under construction will largely proceed", but delays would affect the "next wave" of building through "local fights, slower permitting, and pressure to make data centres pay for their own power".
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: Analysts from the consultancy Oxford Economics have said there are also strong economic incentives for politicians to avoid policies that would severely disrupt data centre construction, pointing to tax revenue and construction jobs they bring.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: Deepak Surana of the Futurum Group, a technology research firm, said he expected there would ultimately be "a negotiation, not a moratorium" from Texas state leaders on data centres to ensure no negative impact on residents' energy and water bills.
sentences.article_title: Did a data centre revolt affect the US mid-term election results?

sentences.text: High above the Arctic, powerful winds usually circle the North Pole each winter, helping trap some of the coldest air on Earth.
sentences.article_title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?

sentences.text: But this circulation, known as the polar vortex, has weakened and shifted position in recent days.
sentences.article_title: Could the earliest weakening of the polar vortex on record bring UK snow?

sentences.text: While such disruptions can occur during winter, scientists say an event this early in November is unprecedented in modern observations.

sentences.text: Businesses should publish salaries in job adverts now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is telling firms, rather than wait for a new law to come in that will force them to do so.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: The government is planning to make pay details compulsory in adverts, with legislation on the issue being brought forward "as soon as possible".
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: It argues the change will help jobseekers, particularly those applying for their first job, and could help prevent pay discrimination.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: However, one industry group said setting pay was a complex process and regulating adverts was not always suitable.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: It comes a week after the UK's equality watchdog said employees should legally be able to find out what their colleagues are earning .
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office launched a consultation into pay and reducing discrimination in the summer, and the government said there had been "overwhelming support" for greater transparency, with 94% of respondents backing the move.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: "Whether you're a young person starting out or a parent trying to support your family, you should know what a job pays before spending your time and effort applying for it," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: The government said the move was part of attempts to reduce the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - ahead of the final report of the Milburn Review into youth inactivity, which is due in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: Publishing salary details upfront could "expose unjustified differences in pay, give workers greater confidence to challenge discrimination and prevent disagreements over pay escalating into disputes".
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: Financial Secretary to the Treasury James Murray told the BBC "this is an important common sense reform".
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: Speaking to Radio 4's Today programme, he said pay "shouldn't be a guessing game" and acknowledged the frustration some might feel when applying for jobs.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: The proposals are similar to measures being introduced in the European Union. , external Employers in Europe will have to disclose the initial pay or range for new roles, which must either be included in a published job advert or shared before an interview.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: According to data from UK jobs website Adzuna , external , 51% of the adverts on its site in September had salary information, but the proportion has been falling in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: Adzuna co-founder Andrew Hunter said being open about pay "should be the norm, not the exception".
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: He added that employers who put a salary on a job advert "attract more applicants, and better-suited ones".
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: Previous research from the CIPD , external , an industry body for human resources managers, has indicated that the public sector and charities are more likely to reveal pay information that private firms, while pay ranges were more common than specific salaries.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: But it found not all employers were "fully transparent", with pay ranges sometimes wider than £10,000.
sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.article_title: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

sentences.text: "There isn't always a single fixed figure, and employers will want to set pay based on a candidate's skills, experience and potential." sentences.text: The head of the Metropolitan Police is to warn that policing in England and Wales is "heading for failure" without urgent reform.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: In a speech on Friday, Sir Mark Rowley will call for the system to change, arguing it is unable to cope with the sophistication of modern criminals.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: He is proposing eight to 10 regional police forces, supported by hundreds of local policing commands and a new National Police Service, in what would be the biggest overhaul since the 1960s.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: The changes would replace the 43-force structure with three tiers: local teams dealing with neighbourhood issues, regional forces sharing specialist resources and a National Police Service tackling the most serious crimes.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: In January it seemed that the many senior police officers were in favour of creating a National Police Service , and that organising into much larger regional forces had won the argument.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood produced a white paper that aligned with their ideas and asked the former Metropolitan Police Commissioner Lord Hogan-Howe to look at what the force boundaries might be.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: But everything changed in July when Andy Burnham became prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: So far, Burnham has not spoken publicly about the plans, and the police chiefs are nervous that they may not have his backing.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: That may be why they have come out so strongly today, warning of the potentially apocalyptic effect of doing nothing.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: As well as pushing hard for large regional forces, they are also making an argument about money which is familiar from the defence funding argument .
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: Sir Mark also pointed out that police funding in England and Wales has fallen from 0.9% of GDP to 0.7%.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: Implicit in that is that while the slice of the cake being allocated to defending the country is growing, the slice being allocated to defending people's communities and their homes is getting smaller.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: In his speech, Sir Mark says organised crime groups, fraud networks, cyber-criminals and those involved in online child abuse increasingly operate across regional and international borders, while police forces remain organised around local areas.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: He will argue that the current system is struggling to keep pace with these threats, saying: "We have 43 overstretched forces trying to do too much, with too little." Merging forces would reduce duplication and could free up thousands of roles to be redirected towards front line policing, he believes.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: Speaking on BBC Breakfast, Sir Mark said crime had changed a lot over the year but the police was largely organised how it was 60 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: "Obviously the world's moved on a long way in that time." His proposals follow a consultation launched by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood in January.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: This included plans for a National Police Service to tackle the most complex crimes and a possible merger of the 43 forces into fewer, larger forces.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: However some rural police and crime commissioners have described the plans as "political manoeuvring" by larger forces to "load the dice in their favour".
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: The Association of Police and Crime Commissioners (APCC) has also questioned whether merging forces is the best way to improve policing.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: It said: "The case for modernisation and a National Police Service is clear.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: The case for reducing 43 forces to nine regional 'mega-forces' is not." Asked on Breakfast what would happen if the reforms were not put in place, Sir Mark said: "the risk is failure".
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: "Failure means solving fewer crimes, less local presence, when you get exceptional incidents like a certain outbreak of disorder like we saw in Hampshire." In September police clashed with anti-migrant protesters in Portsmouth when 120 migrants arrived in a single dinghy.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: "Standing still looks like a degradation of policing day by day, struggling even more as criminals outpace policing because we're not organised to meet it," Sir Mark added.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: "We do need investment as well, but if you threw loads of money at the current system it's still not going to fix the fundamental problem, it's not designed to meet today's challenges," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: "Throwing money at the current system isn't going to work." Sir Mark will use his speech to say that years of underinvestment have left forces relying on ageing technology, and officers are increasingly diverted from neighbourhood policing to deal with other demands, including mental health and social care.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: He will also point to falling police performance, saying positive outcomes nationally are now less than half the level they were 12 years ago, while public confidence has fallen by 9%.
sentences.article_title: Met chief warns policing 'heading for failure' without reform

sentences.text: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order that he says will prevent future presidents from making certain changes to the White House Oval Office.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The executive order declares the president's official office, which he has renovated, to be a national monument.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: "We're making it a national monument, and it will not be allowed to be touched by anybody, destroyed, ripped down by stupid people, in order to build something in a slightly different shape," Trump told reporters on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The order does not prevent future presidents from changing the decor of the famous room.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The document says that it does not "restrict the President's authority to redecorate the monument, select furnishings, or make ordinary operational and security modifications that do not substantially impair the monument's historic structure or architectural character".
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: American presidents currently have the power to make some changes to the White House but large projects require the permission of Congress.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The order comes months after Trump tore down the entirety of the White House East Wing in a project that has faced legal challenges.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The project was not approved by the US Congress.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: It's a symbol of our country and the greatness of our country," Trump said, adding that world leaders who have visited in recent months have complimented his decorative changes to the room.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: Trump said the White House and the Oval Office had been in need of repairs before his changes, calling it "badly damaged".
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: He described broken windows, cracked walls and broken stone.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: Many of the noticeable changes, though, were cosmetic, including a large gold plaque reading "Oval Office" outside the space, paving over the Rose Garden and adding a new helicopter pad.

sentences.text: Trump said the order would "make it impossible for anybody ever to destroy this incredible space".
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: Most executive orders can be overturned and Trump himself scaled back two national monuments in Utah in 2017.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: But revoking a national monument designation has not yet been tested in court.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The White House grounds are already designated as a National Historic Landmark, which is intended to prevent against sudden changes to the building.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: Trump's order calls on the Oval Office to be maintained by the National Park Service "in a manner that protects its historic character, architectural integrity, and association with the Presidency".
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: It notes the existing protections to the White House, but says "nonetheless, the Oval Office merits specific recognition and protective management as a discrete historic structure of national significance".
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: Congress has carved out an exemption to the National Historic Preservation Act, in order to allow presidents to make needed changes.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: The current Oval Office has existed since the early 1930s, after its conception by President Franklin D Roosevelt.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: Greg Werkheiser, from the law firm Cultural Heritage Partners, which specialises in historic preservation, says that temporary alterations like "furniture and decor is completely up to the president's discretion".
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: "As long as they're not damaging the permanent art and architecture, they can generally do whatever they want," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Trump signs order to preserve Oval Office as national monument

sentences.text: A new gold sign was placed outside the Oval Office A Trump administration staff member seen inside the Oval Office in May Werkheiser argues that the Trump administration has shown disregard for other historic sites in Washington and, through lawsuits, has attempted to undermine the laws that require preservation.

sentences.text: He called Trump's order "hypocrisy", noting the various projects he's pushed for across Washington - including plans to build a new triumphal arch, which has been temporarily put on hold by a federal judge.

sentences.text: "On the one hand he's talking about the importance of preserving the Oval Office - which is legally meaningless because he can't do it - and on the other hand he is absolutely taking an axe to the law that allows us to preserve other historic sites." sentences.text: Constables Campbell and Lavery meet newborn baby Benedyct for the second time Two police officers who were first on the scene as a woman gave birth in the back of a car have been reunited with the baby they helped care for.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: They had been taking part in a routine traffic operation in Ballymena, County Antrim, on 9 October when they were approached by the father running towards them.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: Constable Campbell, who has been in the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) for almost two years, said it wasn't something they were expecting.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "I think, obviously, you maybe worry somebody has had a breakdown or somebody needs help, but certainly not that his wife is in labour." Constable Lavery, who joined the PSNI in May 2025, said they had planned to get the mum to the hospital but things moved quicker than expected.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: Lavery said by the time they made it to the car the dad told them that "the baby was coming".
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "She had basically already delivered the baby in the back of the car, she had been absolutely amazing." Campbell says they had been on the night shift when they were approached by the dad along the road For Campbell, what had started as a "very mundane night shift" with "very little happening" had changed dramatically.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: It was half-past-three in the morning, it was raining and it was cold.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: The officers had been on duty on the Raceview Road.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: As Campbell explained, "it's a very exposed piece of road, it wasn't a particularly nice place to be that time of night".
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: Dad of one Lavery was worried about the risks of a birth along the side of the road As a dad himself, Lavery knew there were risks involved, and repeatedly checked with Campbell if the baby had cried.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "We needed that baby to cry," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "And then my colleague said the baby had cried, which was good news, but the worry moved on to mum." All he had on hand was a high-viz jacket that he got from the police car, which he put round the baby and mum to keep them warm.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: Campbell said the mum did all the hard work.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "There was absolutely no hesitation, she lifted the baby up and made sure the baby was ok." He said all they could do was provide a bit of comfort and try to get someone from the Northern Ireland Ambulance Service there as quickly as possible.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: Both police officers have had the opportunity to meet baby Benedyct for the second time this week.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "It was great to go back and see that everybody was doing well," said Campbell.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "He's just so small and dainty and good to get a cuddle off him," explained  Lavery.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: Although he added: " I hope it's not a situation I have to probably be in again." For Campbell, it's something he knows he'll never forget.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "It's the one I'll always remember, it's probably one most people would remember.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: "It's not something that happens, that I've heard of before.
sentences.article_title: Police officers reunite with baby they helped deliver in back of car

sentences.text: A lot of people who have been in the police for years have never experienced it."

sentences.text: The family of six beavers were released into the Loch Ness catchment A family of six beavers have been released into the Loch Ness catchment, 500 years since the species was last recorded there.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The beavers were reintroduced to the Dundreggan rewilding estate in Glenmoriston, having been relocated from elsewhere in Scotland.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The Ness Beaver Project will reintroduce at least 15 beaver family groups into lochs, lochans and rivers around Loch Ness over the next three years.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: Beavers were first reintroduced to Scotland in 2009 after being hunted to extinction about 400 years ago.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The family consists of a mother beaver, two juveniles that are about two years old, and three young beavers who were born earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: NatureScot has approved the release and has granted a licence to Trees for Life and the Beaver Trust.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The project is designed to allow beaver populations to connect and grow in suitable habitat Steve Micklewright, chief executive of Trees for Life, said it was a "very beautiful thing to see" the animals back in their natural habitat.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: He said: "I can see them swimming and very calm, which is a really good sign." He added that the beavers looked "very settled" and relaxed straight away.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The project is designed to allow beaver populations to connect and grow in a suitable habitat, including woodlands and hundreds of miles of river and loch banks.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The beavers came from areas where they were having a negative impact on prime agricultural land and where mitigation measures had not been successful or possible.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The beavers were taken from areas where they were having a negative impact on prime agricultural land The last widely-cited historical record of Scotland's beavers, dating from 1526 to 1527, placed them around Loch Ness.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: Alan McDonnell, head of nature restoration at Trees for Life, said: "The Ness Beaver Project is now set to be a major milestone for nature recovery in Britain.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: It is hoped these will support frogs and dragonflies, with the abundance of insects providing food for birds and bats.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: Trees For Life said that on smaller streams, beaver dams slow the flow of water and trap sediment, helping to improve water quality.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The beavers quickly adapted to their new home Once the animals have settled, the organisation plans to introduce guided tours at Dundreggan, offering opportunities to spot beavers and see signs of their activity.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The River Ness catchment was identified by NatureScot in 2022 as one of the most suitable locations in Scotland for the rodents.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: NatureScot said responses to the applicants' consultation process were positive, with more than 73% of respondents supportive.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: Future release sites will be announced once the beavers have settled into their new environment.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: Before release, the animals underwent health checks at the specialist beaver holding facility at Five Sisters Zoo.
sentences.article_title: 'Major milestone' as beavers released into Loch Ness area

sentences.text: The so-called "quiet quitting" trend where workers do the basic requirements of a job but refuse to do anything more might be hitting the economy, analysis has found.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Over the last decade, Britons have become less engaged with the jobs they do and are less willing to put in extra effort, according to a Resolution Foundation report.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: The thinktank said this could partly help explain the slump in productivity since the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: "This is self-evidently bad for workers, but it also doesn't bode well for productivity and labour supply, both of which are vital for lifting living standards in the years ahead," said Hannah Slaughter, principal economist at the Resolution Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Quiet quitting was popularised on social media shortly after the pandemic .
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Frustrated by high demands, low pay, and a squeeze in living standards, many online posts said workers should only do what their bosses asked and nothing more.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: So you still show up for work, but no more helping out with additional tasks or checking emails outside work hours, instead focusing on work-life balance and "acting your wage".
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Meanwhile, those who were not even "fairly" satisfied with their roles has sunk to one-in-four, the lowest level on record.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: In addition, workers are less likely than 10 years ago to say they have an interesting job, with 63% of those surveyed saying so, down from 74%.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: "Workers today are indeed a little less committed to their employers, and a little less intrinsically drawn to work in general, than workers were a decade ago," the report added.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: This shift over the last decade "may have contributed to weak productivity growth", which has slowed since the financial crisis and weakened again after the pandemic, the Resolution Foundation found.
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Workers were also more focused on pay than in the past, which it said was "perhaps unsurprising... given the flatlining living standards of the past decade".
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: Sir John Curtice, politics professor and co-editor of the report, said the analysis does not mean that young people have "become more 'work-shy', nor have workers in general become more reluctant to change jobs".
sentences.article_title: 'Quiet quitting' could be hitting the economy - here's why

sentences.text: "But if workers are to be fully engaged in their work, it has seemingly become more important for employers to provide jobs that are both financially rewarding and have flexible work hours," he added.

sentences.text: Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood, 25, joined London-based PR agency Fight or Flight in November last year, in the new role of "AI associate" after completing a degree and then a masters in marketing.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: She's part of a recently established, dedicated AI team that has built around 30 AI agents.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Specific tasks include industry research, client reporting, media interview preparation, helping clients create clearer briefs, and image generation.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A big part of Underwood's job is to manage those agents, check their outputs and feed those to the team members who are dealing directly with clients and the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Another key responsibility of hers is to monitor how clients appear in the responses from AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "A huge part is being in client meetings and calls to work out what is actually going to be most helpful from these agents," says Underwood.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: AI is seen as one of the main factors behind graduate job cuts , but companies are also creating dedicated AI-specific graduate roles like Underwood's.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Dillan Patel, for example, joined engineering software company Stride 18 months ago as an intern.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A business management graduate, he was put to work developing an internal chatbot designed to capture the knowledge of a senior staff member transitioning into retirement.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Patel, 24, is now an AI automation analyst, tasked with developing further internal agents to provide specific information to individual teams, while also identifying which manual or repetitive tasks across the company could be done by AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "My role focuses on finding practical ways to use technology, automation, data and AI to improve how we operate," says Coventry-based Patel.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Debra Maxwell is looking for "AI disruptors" Such AI savvy graduates are also in demand from companies like ArvatoConnect, an outsourced contact centre company.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: CEO Debra Maxwell says the company's usual graduate intake is on hold this year, but she plans to resume it next year with a bigger focus on AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We would be looking for more AI-disruptor type roles, where you can challenge us as an organisation to think more holistically about where AI can be applied and where we could grow our business from," says London-based Maxwell.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way." Maxwell adds: "For example, one of our recent graduates is using AI to do deep dives on specific markets, and provide more information for when we're bidding [for new contracts].
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It's basically giving him a more rounded role." If AI can make a graduate job bigger and more integral to the organisation, Maxwell argues that companies can create a more loyal, engaged workforce that is able to contribute more meaningfully, much earlier.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Research from consultancy PwC found that some graduate roles are assuming more responsibilities because of AI, as it allows companies to demand more senior abilities from junior hires.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: For the consultancy's 2026 AI Jobs Barometer , external , it analysed 2.4 million entry-level jobs in the US.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It found that the entry-level roles most influenced by AI are now seven times more likely to require traditionally senior-level skills.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: These include motivational leadership, strategic decision making and team building.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Those entry-level roles with higher expectations have in fact grown 35% since 2019, PwC found, while other entry-level roles actually shrank by 10%.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Cian Clinton uses around ten AI agents for work tasks Cian Clinton, who joined consultancy Valliance last September after graduating from a Bachelor of Science in 2024, says the incorporation of AI into his role makes him feel less like a graduate, and more like an equal team member.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He uses around 10 AI agents daily for different tasks.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Your ideas and your creativity are a lot more valued because you actually get to implement those firsthand, and the responsibility you take on is a lot greater because of that," says London-based Clinton, 23.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I am now taking on responsibilities which would usually take me four or five years to get to." His career progression, he believes, will now be faster as a result.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "AI is killing the 'pyramid' approach…progression is no longer based on your knowledge bank.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Now it's more based on your critical thinking and understanding of the processes," says Clinton.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: There's no doubt Underwood, Patel and Clinton are developing valuable AI knowledge which can help them across their careers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: But with their time at work so focused on AI, does it matter how much - or how little - time they're spending learning about the professional field they're supposed to be operating in?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: The first public words from the prime minister after the American midterm elections were instantly revealing about contemporary international politics and diplomacy.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: "Well, President Trump has accepted the results," Andy Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: It is not an observation British leaders have frequently had to make about recent American presidents - that they are not disputing the result of elections in their own country.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: But what would previously have been taken for granted no longer can be.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Burnham remains in the foothills of establishing a relationship with the president – so far it has amounted to a handful of phone calls and one face-to-face meeting at the United Nations in New York in September.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: As he continues to attempt to build a rapport with Donald Trump, he will be doing so with a president in a wildly different political situation than when Sir Keir Starmer was trying to build bridges with him.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: No longer is this a story of an extraordinary comeback, but of a midterm president seemingly punished for the consequences of a foreign war the type of which he had originally promised to avoid.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Time to focus on cost of living, says PM after US election results Trump's loss limits powers at home, but it will likely be different abroad And it is noticeable that the British government's public reaction is grounded too in the consequences of the war with Iran: the cost of living.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: "I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all and that's the cost of living," the prime minister said.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: And, bluntly, it is one that puts many, including many of America's allies, in alignment with many in America, Democrat and Republican, who when asked why these elections went as they did, point at the prices displayed outside any petrol station.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Speaking before the votes in America were counted, the Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband reflected on this when I spoke to him on BBC Newscast , external .
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: When I asked him specifically if he feared that a domestically humiliated Trump may prove more belligerent internationally, it was to the Iran war the foreign secretary referred.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: "We know that we need a diplomatic way out of this conflict, and so that is one of the things that we're working on.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: It's something I talked to the US Secretary of State about at the G20, and it's something we continue to work on," he added.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: The foreign secretary met Marco Rubio at the meeting in Atlanta last week.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: But the big question for the British government, and so many others, is does defeat at home make it more likely that President Trump gets angrier abroad?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Or, do America's traditional allies, the UK, the European Union, Canada, Australia and others feel more strident and willing to work with Donald Trump's domestic political opponents to try to challenge and restrain a weakened president?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: The answers to these two final questions will determine much in world affairs in the next couple of years.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: The US elections will change Trump - how will Burnham react?

sentences.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood set out the plans in the House of Commons Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has set out plans to overhaul immigration rules.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Proposals for stricter requirements to qualify for permanent settlement in the UK were first outlined in detail in November 2025, when Mahmood was home secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: She has argued that settlement should be "earned", rather than being granted automatically, with those who contribute more to the country able to settle fastest.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Following a consultation , external , Mahmood has now announced her final decision on what changes should be taken forward.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Elements of her original proposals have been revised following a backlash from some Labour MPs, with plans to make foreign care workers already in the UK wait 15 years to qualify for settlement scrapped.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes Indefinite leave to remain (ILR) – also known as settlement – gives someone the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under the current system, people with ILR can also apply for benefits if they are eligible.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: People who have lived in the UK for 12 months after being given ILR can apply for British citizenship, if they also meet other requirements , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under the government's plans, the standard length of time migrants will have to live in the UK to qualify for permanent settlement will double from five to 10 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under this 10-year pathway, applicants must have earned at least £12,571 for five of the seven years immediately before being granted settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Migrants who have claimed certain benefits or breached immigration rules will only be able to settle after at least 20 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Adults with a criminal record will be refused settlement, with discretion to refuse cases where the offence was committed when the applicant was under 18.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Refugees who arrived in the UK through an official government scheme will qualify for settlement after five years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: However, other refugees will need to wait 10 years and either work or study.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Those who do not work or study will need to wait 20 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Refugees who arrived in the UK by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they don't.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: The changes will apply to migrants who are already in the UK but not those who have already been granted settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: A partner who arrives with someone who then applies for ILR will be able to settle at the same time, as long as they meet the relevant requirements.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: However, a partner who joins later will need to complete the same qualifying residence period before they are eligible for settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Eligible couples will be able to combine their earnings to meet the minimum income  requirement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: The household income threshold will be £25,142 – twice the individual minimum income requirement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The aim is to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: These cancers are often found only after they have spread.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The tests look for proteins or fragments of DNA in the blood that may signal cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Results could help doctors decide which patients with vague symptoms need further investigations.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: More than 20,000 patients aged 45 and over with symptoms such as pain or persistent bloating will be eligible to take part.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The government-funded trial, led by the University of Birmingham, will assess whether the tests are accurate enough for wider NHS use.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The idea of a blood test that can identify multiple cancers is not new.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A separate NHS trial of a test called Galleri recently failed to meet its main goal of reducing diagnoses of late-stage cancers, although researchers are still assessing its potential benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Prof Peter Johnson, NHS England's national clinical director for cancer, said detecting abdomen cancer early was "notoriously difficult" because symptoms can easily be mistaken for other less serious conditions.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Earlier diagnosis gives patients a much better chance of successful treatment and survival.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Around 71,000 people in England are diagnosed each year with pancreatic, stomach, liver, ovarian or bowel cancer, and nearly 35,000 die from these diseases.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The new STRIDE-RCT trial , external is about detecting bowel, small bowel, stomach, oesophageal, pancreatic, liver, bile duct and gallbladder, ovarian, endometrial, kidney, bladder and prostate cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Patients will provide one or two tubes of blood, taken at their GP practice, alongside routine tests.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Scientists will then analyse the samples for signs of cancer and, if present, may be able to pinpoint where in the body the tumour is located.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A positive result does not automatically mean there is cancer, and a negative result is not a guaranteed all-clear.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Michelle Mitchell from Cancer Research UK said: "GPs have long needed better tools to help them navigate that uncertainty by identifying which patients require further testing and this trial in England is an important step towards addressing that need."
