sentences.text: Eating fruit and vegetable scraps such as peels and stalks could provide a health boost that most of us are missing, say UK researchers , external .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: They say scraps are an overlooked source of dietary fibre and are encouraging people to try "root-to-tip" eating, including watermelon rind, pineapple core and butternut squash seeds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Most adults do not get enough fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Official figures , external show only 4% meet the recommended 30g a day, despite its well-known benefits for gut health.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Fibre aids digestion, helps you feel fuller for longer and is linked to a lower risk of heart disease and bowel cancer. , external Skin and pips can be beneficial, the fibre researchers say As a rule of thumb, the skins of fruit and veg pack more fibre than the insides.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Eating a kiwi with the skin on , external provides 50% more fibre than having a peeled one, for example.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: For their study, the scientists at King's College London analysed 12 raw or uncooked fresh foods - beetroot, bell pepper, broccoli, butternut squash, cauliflower, celeriac, curly kale, fennel, kiwi fruit, leek, pineapple and watermelon.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Project lead Dr Rachel Gibson said the findings suggested people are throwing away a significant amount of fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "This isn't just a nutritional loss, it's also a financial one - you're effectively throwing away a substantial portion of what you've paid for." King's College London has been experimenting in its canteen , external , offering staff and students root-to-tip meals, such as banana skin curry.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: At home, people might want to try leaving skins on kiwi fruit, using broccoli stalks in stir-fries or adding bell pepper seeds to dishes, the researchers suggest.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: While cooking can change the fibre content, it doesn't usually destroy it all.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Steaming, microwaving or quick sautéing tends to preserve nutrients best .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Gibson said: "This isn't about perfection and this isn't about forcing people to eat unpalatable food – it's about recognising the nutritional value in components we've been conditioned to discard." She acknowledges some may be hesitant to try it.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some diners raised concerns during the canteen trial.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Over the nine-week period, "root-to-tip" dishes made up a third of total daily hot menu sales at the university.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Those choosing the new dishes were less likely to finish their meals than diners eating from the conventional menu.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Kirsten Jackson, a dietitian with the British Dietetic Association who specialises in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), says the food hacks are useful as long as produce is washed thoroughly.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She suggests blending pineapple cores into smoothies, but says the tough skins are not something she would recommend.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some stalks may need to be cooked or finely chopped to make them more palatable, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "Just because a broccoli stalk doesn't fit into tonight's meal doesn't mean it needs to go in the bin.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Chop it up, freeze it and add it to a soup or stir-fry another day," she said.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She advises increasing fibre intake gradually to avoid bloating, noting that people who have IBS may find it harder to tolerate.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: And there are some things to avoid entirely, said the British Nutrition Foundation.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Green potatoes and rhubarb leaves contain toxic compounds, while tough stalks and seeds may not be suitable for young children.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: "My low Vitamin D levels hit me like a truck" Twenty-three-year-old Saskia Reeves-Priestley was at work when she suddenly collapsed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I just felt really dizzy, really nauseous, was having heart palpitations and was really hot," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia, a special educational needs teacher, was a keen goalkeeper who played football four times a week and felt fit and healthy.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Blood tests later showed her level was so low - it was "next to nothing".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, low vitamin D rates are increasing in some age groups , external - particularly in girls and young women.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Lower levels of sunlight - depending on where in the world you live or the time of year - decrease the body's ability to produce it.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Doctors don't routinely offer blood tests to check for vitamin D deficiency, but will offer a supplement if a patient is concerned they might be high risk.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to the bone disease rickets in babies and infants.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In adults it causes a similar weakening of the bone called osteomalacia , external .
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "They call it the silent disease," says Dr Suma Uday, a paediatric endocrinologist who wants to raise awareness of the problem.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She warns that vitamin D deficiency in young people and adults is difficult to spot and can be missed or misdiagnosed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Symptoms include fatigue and joint and bone pain.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday says: "It's basically silently eating away at the bones, leaving them softened and prone to breaks." Amaka Osu says she doesn't think many of her friends realise what the symptoms are Amaka was in the middle of making dinner at her university house in Liverpool when she started shaking.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I couldn't really see in front of me," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Her housemate took her to A&E - later she too would be diagnosed as vitamin D deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Other than feeling tired, she says she had no symptoms: "I'm a 21-year-old student.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: I've got work and uni - I'm always feeling tired." She remembers her mother suffering from low vitamin D but says she did not realise it could happen to her.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: After taking supplements, Amaka feels a lot better, but she is anxious in case it happens again.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "It was scary and I don't want to experience that again." Uday joins other clinicians and academics who have formed a group - ACT NOW Vitamin D - calling for the threshold at which you are classified as deficient to be raised.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She says that would "catch" more people with low vitamin D and give a more accurate picture of how widespread the issue is.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: It would also mean they can treat the deficiency earlier, she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday warns of "a lifelong deficit" in women - in adolescence, then pregnancy, and then the newborn is affected.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If you don't correct it from the very beginning," she says, "this is going to affect multiple generations." Saskia Reeves-Priestley plays football four times a week - and had no previous symptoms "It's shocking," says Prof Martin Hewison, from the University of Birmingham.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: He tells me that despite being 100 years on from the discovery of vitamin D "rickets hasn't gone away".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If we have rickets in the community, there are going to be many more people who are vitamin D deficient." He says the government should look into wider fortification of food in which vitamins are added to foods during production.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Countries like Canada and Sweden have mandatory policies.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, some foods such as breakfast cereals and spreads are already fortified with vitamin D, but it is voluntary.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: During the winter months, people start to lose their vitamin D levels.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "We might have to accept that for certain groups vitamin D supplementation is a matter of course," says Hewison.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia is now taking vitamin D supplements regularly - and is back in goal.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Patients in many parts of the country have been left unable to access their GP surgery online after a tech firm went into administration.

sentences.text: Silicon Practice ran digital services, including websites, online booking and consultations, for around 500 practices in England – just under 10% of the total.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Practices across the country, including in London, Gloucestershire and Norfolk , have reported problems.

sentences.text: Services in Wales are also affected.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: GP leaders said the problem would cause huge disruption, given the scale of online booking that now takes places.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Patients in areas that are affected are being advised they will have to make appointments via the phone.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Since last year , all practices in England have had to offer online appointment booking.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: Currently, more than 40% of appointments are made that way.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm

sentences.text: "If your GP practice website is unavailable and you need help, you should contact your practice by phone or in person as usual." Affected practices have been contacted by NHS England with advice on how to maintain business continuity and minimise the impact on patient care.

sentences.text: "When websites are not working, it can be hugely disruptive for patients and place additional pressures on already stretched practice teams.

sentences.text: Consultant doctors in England are to stage a two-day strike next month in a dispute over pay and working conditions.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The walkout will begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: This is known as Christmas Day cover and is likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Consultants – the most senior doctors in hospitals – were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In a joint statement, BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta, said they had tried to negotiate with the government in "good faith", but "time-and-time again ministers have kicked the can down the road".
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, that road has now run out, and we have been forced to announce strikes.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Consultants take their responsibilities incredibly seriously, and striking does not come naturally, but we are hearing loud and clear from the profession that they have had enough." Average earnings for consultants top £150,000 a year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Basic pay starts at £113,500, with the most experienced getting £150,500.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But many earn tens of thousands in extra payments and awards.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In the strike ballot, 76% of consultants who took part voted in favour of strike action, with just over half of eligible BMA members taking part.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The government says this represents only around one in five consultants employed by the NHS in England voting for strike action, as nearly half are not BMA members.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the government had been in "constructive discussions" with the BMA so it was "disappointing" the strike dates had been announced.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: She said taking strike action would be "irresponsible" and "place the health service under even greater pressure".
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The strike announcement comes as consultants and other doctors are taking part in strike action during November in Northern Ireland .
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Consultants last took strike action in England in 2023.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The long-running dispute involving resident doctors in England came to an end earlier this year after more than three years of on-and-off strike action.

sentences.text: Dr Sarah Redvers brought a claim of constructive dismissal A doctor who raised concerns about the treatment of children questioning their gender has told the BBC she was accused of transphobia, bullied and harassed out of her child protection job in the NHS.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Dr Sarah Redvers, who was a named safeguarding GP, said she faced a brutal investigation after she passed on complaints brought to her by other doctors.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Speaking publicly for the first time, Redvers said she felt she was "silenced" for doing her job after questioning whether another GP was appropriately assessing the needs of young people who were distressed about their gender identity.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: She has brought a claim of constructive dismissal against the NHS Sussex Integrated Care Board (ICB), which managed health services in the county, and Adam Doyle, who was the ICB's chief executive until 2025.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Redvers told a three-week employment tribunal hearing that she felt the focus on investigating her meant issues of patient safety had been sidelined.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Dozens of children put at risk after gender care failures at GP clinic, inquiry finds Unacceptable waits for adult gender clinic appointments, review says "I was just bewildered really that the medical and safeguarding issues were completely lost," she said.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: "It's really risky," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: NHS Surrey and Sussex said: "We recognise that some employment processes should have been handled differently." They have apologised to Redvers.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: In June 2026, nearly six years after she first raised concerns, a separate NHS safety investigation found that dozens of children, some as young as 13, had been inappropriately prescribed drugs at the WellBN practice , the clinic where the other doctor worked.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: The report said 78 children had potentially been harmed after puberty-blocking drugs and cross sex hormones were prescribed to them without proper checks.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: The report said it was in response to a drug review carried out in autumn 2024, not to the concerns first raised by Redvers years earlier.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Redvers, who has many years of experience working with vulnerable groups, was a named safeguarding GP for Sussex, which meant other doctors who had safety concerns about patients could turn to her for advice and help.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: The tribunal heard that in July 2020, a doctor got in touch because she was worried about a patient who had gone to an online clinic which was registered overseas.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: It wanted the GP to take over prescribing testosterone to a vulnerable 18-year-old female, who was distressed about her gender.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: The doctor was also given advice on such prescriptions by a Brighton GP, Dr Sam Hall.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: "The concerns to me were that Hall was recommending treatment for patients that he hadn't assessed, that he hadn't met, and that other GPs were uncomfortable with prescribing," Redvers said.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Redvers spoke to NHS England (NHSE) and was advised to make the complaint as a whistleblower.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: It was investigated and NHSE said it was satisfied with Hall's practice.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Over the following months several other GPs voiced their concerns to Redvers about the quality of assessments, the prescription of puberty blocking drugs and cross sex hormones, and the lack of specialist supervision at the WellBN clinic, where Hall was based.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Again, the NHS investigated her concerns.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: She said she was also told by the investigator that there was a "general worry" that there "would be allegations of transphobia." Hall, who is a trans man and was born female, qualified as a GP in 2019 and is known as a campaigner for transgender rights in Brighton.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Publicly, he had said that his own pain had shown him the importance of "affirmative care" - support for a patient in a way which accepts rather than challenges their preferred gender and treatment decisions follow from that.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: He was also working with the NHS locally on setting up a Trans Health hub and with a Brighton trans support charity called The Clare Project.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: The second NHS investigation considered "the full scope" of Hall's work and concluded there was no cause for concern.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: It also said there was "one colleague whose persistent interest in the issue appeared disproportionate." Redvers took that to mean her.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: The concerns she said she and others were raising were about the quality of care being provided, and whether it had the necessary medical evidence to underpin it, not her views on gender.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: "It's about medical assessment and treatment of patients, which is something we have to get right, particularly in this complex group of vulnerable patients," she said.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: She said she viewed any suggestion of transphobia as "appalling," and it was "dangerous" that such claims were obscuring the medical and safeguarding issues she was raising.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: In 2021, whilst waiting for the outcome of the second investigation and prompted by a concern raised by local mental health services about the care of a vulnerable 15-year-old, Redvers referred Hall to the medical regulator, the GMC.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Hall emailed Adam Doyle, then CEO of NHS Sussex, directly to complain.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: "I am being victimised here, and I need proper protection from this individual and their repeated attempts to disrupt my career" he said.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Adam Doyle, was chief executive of the NHS Sussex Integrated Care Board until 2025 Although Doyle at first denied to the tribunal he knew Hall before this, it emerged during the tribunal that he had previously had a number of mentoring meetings with the GP.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: The GMC investigation was not taken forward.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: However, the NHS launched an investigation into Redvers, bringing in an external investigator.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: The tribunal heard she was called to what she described as a "brutal" four-hour interrogation.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: "It was oppressive, very upsetting.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: I didn't feel I had the chance at all to explain what had happened," she said.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: "I broke down at one point".
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: She said she was off sick for several months as a result and received treatment for trauma.
sentences.article_title: GP says she was forced out of job after raising concerns about gender treatment

sentences.text: Other colleagues who were interviewed as part of the investigation into Redvers also complained about the process and the NHS upheld most of their complaints.

sentences.text: Laura gave birth to her son Arthur in 2018 "Women, since the beginning of time, have birthed and looked after children and I just couldn't be bothered.

sentences.article_title: 'The veil of shame around postnatal depression needs to go'

sentences.text: The NHS says postnatal depression , external , also known as postpartum depression, is a "common" mental health condition that can happen after having a baby.
sentences.article_title: 'The veil of shame around postnatal depression needs to go'

sentences.text: "Postnatal depression can happen to anyone and this is why the veil of shame needs to come down, through education or through listening to people," said Laura.

sentences.article_title: 'The veil of shame around postnatal depression needs to go'

sentences.article_title: 'The veil of shame around postnatal depression needs to go'

sentences.article_title: 'The veil of shame around postnatal depression needs to go'

sentences.article_title: 'The veil of shame around postnatal depression needs to go'

sentences.article_title: 'The veil of shame around postnatal depression needs to go'

sentences.text: There, Laura received 10 weeks of specialist inpatient care which she said had made all the difference.

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools and colleges in England will be required to recognise antisemitism as a distinct category of harm and take explicit action against it.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It means anti-Jewish hatred will be treated as a specific safeguarding risk rather than being dealt with through existing measures to stop racism and bullying.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The government has accepted all of the 27 recommendations made in the government-commissioned review including dedicated training for teachers and more consistent recording of incidents.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says The review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England was led by former Ofsted chief inspector Sir David Bell and presented to Parliament on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC it marked a "generational moment" to re-educate young people, among whom she said the issue of antisemitism was "particularly prevalent".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the House of Commons "teachers should not bring their own political views into the classroom" but they should not avoid discussing important topics.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review was launched following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025, in which two men were killed.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Separate reviews were also commissioned into antisemitism in healthcare and into public order and hate crime laws.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters .
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also recommends that the government sets up a type of hotline where school leaders can access immediate advice on tackling antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Bell, who is now vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, heard evidence from pupils, teachers, governors and parents across state and independent schools, as well as from community organisations.

sentences.text: He told the BBC: "This is not just a report for Jewish children in Jewish schools.

sentences.text: The maternity unit at the Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital could become the only one in the county The Royal College of Midwives (RCM) said it was concerned by reports that two maternity units could close.

sentences.text: Norfolk has maternity units at hospitals in Norwich, Gorleston and King's Lynn, with the latter two also serving Cambridgeshire and Suffolk.

sentences.text: The trade union posted on Facebook , external that local maternity services should be invested in rather than cut.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group (NWUHG) has set out its "Case for Change" , external on how services could be delivered in future, but stressed that no decisions had been made and no consultation had begun.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: NHS leaders said any move to concentrate services at one or two sites would be based on providing safer care for women and babies.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: Documents show , external that some women that would currently give birth in Gorleston would face a two-hour public transport journey to get to alternative hospitals The BBC also understands the health secretary is talking to the chief executive of NHS England regarding what has been happening in Norfolk.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: The RCM warned that closing units serving rural and isolated communities could mean women travelling "unacceptable distances" while in labour.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: If maternity services were removed, the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group (NWUHG) said that neonatal units and children's inpatient wards would also close because the services were inter-dependent.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: Options include keeping services as they are, or closing consultant-led maternity units at the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston, the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King's Lynn, or both.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: As well as women in Norfolk, the plans could affect women in Lowestoft and north Suffolk who give birth in Gorleston and those in Wisbech and north-east Cambridgeshire who travel to King's Lynn.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: The RCM argued the proposals risked worsening existing inequalities in maternity outcomes and said the answer was investment and more staffing, rather than allowing services to "shrink".
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: It also said closures could result in midwives being redeployed further from home.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: The Case for Change argues that falling birth rates, workforce shortages and increasing numbers of women requiring more complex care are making it harder to sustain specialist services at every site.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: Lesley Dwyer, NWUHG chief executive and a former midwife, previously told the BBC the review was one of the most significant pieces of work undertaken by the organisation and was aimed at making services sustainable in the long term.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: "The scenarios examined so far are a starting point for further assessment, not formal proposals," she said.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: "No preferred approach has been identified and no decision has been made to close or relocate these services.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: "Patient safety must remain at the centre of this work.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: We also need to understand what different approaches could mean for choice, travel, access and the experiences of women, babies, children and families." The work comes after NHS bosses said that smaller maternity units across the country may have to close.
sentences.article_title: Midwives concerned over possible baby unit closures

sentences.text: Ofcom has set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Under the UK's social media ban - which is due to come into force in March next year - those under that age will be prevented from accessing ten of the biggest platforms, including Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Many UK adults are also likely to have to confirm that they are not under-age by using one of the proposed measures, which are subject to government approval.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: A similar ban was introduced in Australia last year but many children there have found ways to get round it .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: The UK says it intends to take a tougher approach.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Age verification below 18 is challenging because 16 and 17 year olds don't have credit cards or full driving licences, and may not have passports either.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: They can also look significantly older or younger than they are.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: However, ultimately it will be up to the tech companies to figure out how to implement the checks: the onus is on social network providers to come up with their own solutions and comply.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Meta told the BBC it already applies some methods recommended by Ofcom to enforce its user age requirements or place users in Teen Accounts settings.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But it said applying age checks at device-level, via app stores, could reduce the burden on people to have to repeatedly verify their age across multiple platforms.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: This would place responsibility with Apple and Google, who between them operate most of the world's smartphones.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Apple has already introduced age verification in the UK .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: However Ofcom says that would not absolve the social network providers from doing their own checks as well.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Dawes said making the ban work would be a joint effort.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "At Ofcom, what we will do is make sure that the services that the social media companies put in the checks that they need to," she told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "That's our job, but the wider question about how everybody engages with this, it is for everybody, really.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Child safety campaigners including the Molly Rose Foundation and NSPCC welcomed Ofcom's guidance.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But both said there were lessons to be learned from how Australia's social media ban had been implemented, after it was found many under-16s could still access social platforms .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "That's why, as we prepare to embark on our own social media ban in the UK, we need to make sure we accurately know the age of child users," said Rani Govender, head of child safety online at the NSPCC.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: She said the government and Ofcom must ensure tech firms are held accountable for meeting age check standards "to help keep children safe online and ensure the ban delivers change in practice".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But Andy Burrows, the Molly Rose Foundation's chief executive, said Ofcom had shown a "dire track record" of enforcing the Online Safety Act - raising questions over how effectively it would help deliver a social media ban.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "Andy Burnham must deliver a ban that learns the lessons from Australia and that incentivises safety-by-design as the price of admission to the UK market, with a ban as the starting point in a proper plan to give children a safe and happy online life," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Jonny Bunt, corporate affairs director of BT's consumer division, said families should "prepare children for life online after the ban and highlight the risks of trying to dodge the restrictions".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "Having those conversations now and giving young people time to prepare for the changes in March will be crucial in helping them adapt to a significant change for a whole generation," he said.

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.

sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: This vast machine at the European Laboratory for Particle Physics (Cern) on the Swiss-French border smashes atoms together to break them apart and discover what is inside them.

sentences.text: The result is important because it could help researchers develop a new, more complete theory of how the Universe works.

sentences.text: Many sub-atomic particles are created by smashing the insides of atoms together Dark matter makes up a large part of our cosmos, and yet researchers have struggled to detect it.

sentences.text: Scientists know it is there because its gravitational force influences normal matter, but in all other respects it has remained completely invisible.

sentences.text: So in this experiment, particles were smashed together at high energy and scientists studied the material that was thrown out - the shrapnel of collisions.

sentences.text: One of these is a sub-atomic particle - smaller than an atom - called a beauty quark.
sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.article_title: Scientists detect signals at the smallest scale ever explored

sentences.text: Forever chemicals - or PFAS - can enter the human body after leaking into soil and waterways The government is launching its first study into the levels of so-called 'forever chemicals' in the UK population.
sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.text: By taking blood and urine samples, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) hopes to gain a better understanding of any potential health risks caused by the substances also known as PFAS, as well as other potential contaminants like lead and arsenic.
sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.text: It said current evidence suggested the possible health impacts associated with PFAS are likely to be limited, but said the strongest links found in large population groups have been to raised cholesterol and lower birth weights.

sentences.text: The first results are expected next year.
sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.text: PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) have been used prolifically since the 1940s and 1950s because they are resistant to water, oil and heat.

sentences.text: It is why they have been placed in thousands of items such as pots and pans, clothing and foams used to fight fires.
sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.text: But because they do not break down easily in the environment  - hence the name 'forever chemicals' - they have raised health concerns in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.text: Two are already banned in the UK - PFOA and PFOS - because prolonged exposure to them can increase the risk of cancer, according to the World Health Organization. , external But the study of PFAS is an emerging field with more than 15,000 types to research.
sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.text: The UKHSA will take blood and urine samples collected through the existing Health Survey for England , external to establish baseline levels of PFAS, lead, arsenic, bisphenols, phthalates and flame retardants in the population.

sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.article_title: Major study into 'forever chemicals' in people's bodies launched in UK

sentences.text: Cetirizine is commonly used to relieve allergy symptoms Kenyan pharmacists have warned women against inserting allergy tablets into their vaginas in an attempt to make them tighter, following the spread of potentially dangerous medical advice on social media.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: The warning follows a wave of social media posts promoting cetirizine - a widely available oral antihistamine used to treat allergies - as a way of tightening the vagina, supposedly to enhance sexual pleasure.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: Although antihistamines can sometimes cause dryness as a side effect, experts say this does not strengthen vaginal muscles.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: "Dryness is not tightness... instead, it may increase friction, discomfort, and the risk of tissue injury," the Pharmaceutical Society of Kenya (PSK) said.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: "Inserting oral tablets is unsafe.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: Cetirizine tablets are made to be swallowed.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: Their ingredients have not been tested on delicate vaginal tissue," it added.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: Cetirizine is commonly used to relieve symptoms such as sneezing, a runny nose, itchy eyes and skin reactions, including hives.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: The controversy began earlier this week when posts circulated on TikTok claiming that cetirizine could reduce vaginal moisture and create a sensation of tightness during sex.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: This sparked widespread debate, with some users promoting the practice while others questioned its safety.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: There have also been local media reports of the price of the drug rising and increased demand in some pharmacies, especially in the capital, Nairobi.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: "Cetirizine is an allergy medicine, taken by mouth.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: It is not approved or tested for any other purpose, and definitely not for vaginal use," the PSK, a professional body representing pharmacists in Kenya, said in a statement issued on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: "If you have already tried it.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: See a doctor if you have pain, bleeding, burning, itching, unusual discharge, or fever," it advised.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: The society also urged social media influencers and content creators to take care when sharing health information, saying that unverified claims could put people's health at risk.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: The warning comes a day after Kenya's health ministry expressed concern about the trend.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: Ouma Oluga, a senior health official, said some social media users appeared to be treating the medical advice from experts as a joke, without considering the possible consequences.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: He suggested that the authorities could introduce a system to track the distribution and purchase of medicines to help identify possible misuse.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: However, no formal decision has been announced on such a initiative.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: The PSK said it was aware of reports of increased demand for cetirizine, rising prices and shortages at some pharmacies.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: It urged retailers not to exploit the trend, warning that people who genuinely needed the medicine for allergies could struggle to obtain it.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: It went on to encourage its members not to knowingly dispense medicines that would be misused - and report any side affects to the health authorities of those that had been.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: The PSK ended its statement by saying that unverified online trends should never trump what the experts say: "Check with a pharmacist before using any medicine for a purpose it was not made for.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan pharmacists warn against viral craze of using allergy drug for vaginal tightening

sentences.text: "Do not rely on social media for medical advice." sentences.text: Mackenzie was found guilty in October of the murder of 190 children A Kenyan court is sentencing the leader of a doomsday cult, Paul Mackenzie, after his conviction for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Alongside 27 others, Mackenzie was found guilty of the murders for instructing members of his cult to starve their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in Shakahola forest near the Kenyan coast.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The sprawling investigation into the cases shocked Kenya and drew international attention.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Ahead of sentencing, prosecutors in the court in Mombasa had argued for the death penalty for Mackenzie because of the gravity of the crimes.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The prosecutors also cited what they described as Mackenzie's lack of remorse for the crimes.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: They requested life sentences for his co-accused.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Mackenzie and the co-accused have formally pleaded for mercy and asked for leniency from the court.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Before their conviction on 19 October, they had all pleaded not guilty and repeatedly insisted that nobody was forced to die.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Mackenzie's followers believed he was "Jesus's mouthpiece", Justice Diana Mochache said as she delivered her eight-hour judgement last month.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Those who opposed Mackenzie's teachings were beaten to death.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: One of his co-accused said he had told his followers that anyone who "resisted the directive to fast must be forced to go to heaven through kicks and blows".
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Burials inside the forest where the cult was based were called "weddings" and those who died "were celebrated as having wedded with Jesus" the judge said.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The judge found that the deaths arose from an organised system, including religious teachings and directives that compelled followers to follow the deadly fasting.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Post-mortem results showed the cause of deaths to be starvation for most victims, while others died from suffocation, strangulation or head injuries.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The cause of death could not be determined for some, with their bodies having decomposed, while others died soon after their rescue as they were so emaciated.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: More than 400 bodies were dug up in Shakahola forest The Shakahola deaths have shone a spotlight on the lack of oversight of rogue religious activities and how they could have carried on for so long.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The gravity of the case prompted President William Ruto to set up a commission of inquiry, although this was later declared unconstitutional.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Investigations by the state-funded Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) revealed that local administration and law enforcement officials had repeatedly turned a blind eye to the cult's activities.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The cult leader had previously been arrested and later released for lack of evidence.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Mackenzie established Good News International Ministries in 2003.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Over the next 16 years, the church grew in popularity, drawing thousands of followers in its branches across Kenya.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The church ran a television station called Times TV which would broadcast his sermons from his church in Malindi.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: His End Days sermons included conspiracy theories that described education as "evil", healthcare as "against the doctrine" and digital identity cards as "the mark of the devil".
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: The main church shut down in 2019 and Mackenzie moved to Shakahola forest, encouraging his devotees to follow him.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: While the conclusion of the murder cases may bring a sense of justice for the victims and their families, the convictions only account for 191 victims, while more than 400 bodies were exhumed from the forest.
sentences.article_title: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader who murdered 191 people

sentences.text: Elections are scheduled for 2028, but Tshisekedi has warned that fighting in the east could delay voting.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: Against this backdrop, Kabila has questioned whether elections alone can resolve the country's political crisis.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: "Does Congo need elections or a revolution?" he asked, arguing that lasting peace required a fundamental overhaul of the country's executive and legislature.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: International security analyst Ovigwe Eguegu argues that Kabila is banking on military force to regain political influence, while Tshisekedi seems to be trying to extend his time in office beyond what the constitution allows.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader

sentences.text: "It looks like the Congolese people are going to lose either way, because neither of these two sides present a credible economic transformation plan for both the eastern Congo and the entirety of the country," Eguegu said.
sentences.article_title: Suited and booted: How Joseph Kabila went from president to rebel leader
